utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-97-25-T, the Prosecutor versus Milorad Krnojelac.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Peggy Kuo on behalf of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Good to see you again. And, Mr. Bakrac, you too.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon. Mihajlo Bakrac for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And, Mr. Krnojelac, are you able to hear the proceedings in a language which you are able to understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I can hear it, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It's good to see you here too. This is a Status Conference called in accordance with Rule 65 ter. I think, Mr. Bakrac, I should ask you is there anything you want to raise relating to the mental and physical condition of your client?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I had an opportunity to talk to my client and -- well, before this Status Conference, and I sincerely hope that both the mental and physical state of my client have been preserved, even though I think that everybody is clear about the uncertainty between now and the sentencing date. It does have an effect. So I would appreciate if we could have at least a time frame within which we could expect the judgement to come down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Bakrac, if I gave you some indication and then we didn't live up to it, your client would be even more disappointed. I can assure you we have been hard at work. It has not been an easy judgement to write, mainly because of the immense number of incidents, which we have been very careful to look at individually. But it is getting close. That's the best I think I should say. If I say any more, your client, I think, would be distressed if we were later than we said we anticipated. Is there anything else you want to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, everything else is fine, as far as what I have talked about, my client, regarding his mental and physical state. And I already mentioned his anticipation. So that's all, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And the fact that he has become a little more hirsute than he was before by growing a mustache, that is not any indication, I hope, of his mental state having deteriorated. Is there anything that the Prosecution wants to raise, Ms. Kuo?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well, then. Well, we are grateful to you all for coming. It is unfortunate that you haven't got a judgement yet, and we understand that, but we have been working very hard. I assure you the next time that we see you it will not necessarily be for sentencing, Mr. Bakrac, as you suggested. It will be for judgement and, according to what the judgement is, also sentencing. Well, we shall see you then. I'll adjourn now.
